evidence: Cic. Clu. 29: quem ōdisse jam nōn potestis (Lewis & Short s.v. jam)
terms.comment: Says that something has stopped being so: jam nōn pluit, it’s not raining any more. So nihil jam, nothing any more; nēmō jam, nobody any more.
Of something that will not go on: nōn diūtius manēbō, I won't stay any longer.

phrases.latin: Theodōrus olīvam ē catīnō gustāvit, quae jam amāra nōn erat
phrases.english: Theo tasted an olive from the dish, which was no longer bitter
phrases.source: Libellus III, Apud avum et aviam

sources: Lewis & Short: jam · Lewis & Short: diu
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 76, 88, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
